chapter: Billie Holiday with the band (1971 session)
title: Riffraff dates, uniforms and rubber bands on the horns
summary: Basie refuses to call any place that pays him a dive and says players still use rubber bands on horns when springs break.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Did you play a lot of riffraff during
that year?
What is riffraff?
You know, kind of crummy?
Real crummy places, dives.
I don't know what they are.
Are you being difficult.
(Laught=er.)
Well, I don't call no place a riffraff that pays me.
Ah, very well said, very well said.
She said that you used to alternate riffraff joints and then you'd play some good white hotel and that you'd go from one extreme to the other. Is that true?
(Laughter.)
I have spoken.
Okay. You didn't have the right uniforms, clothes or equipment.
I didn't have what, dear ?
The band didn't have the right uniforms or clothes or equipment.
What would we work in, overalls?
(Laughter.)
How about the horns? Did you ever see -- did Prez's horn have rubber bands?
Well, I guess maybe (inaudible).
Yeah, was that part of the problem at the beginning? I mean, when you say --
Let me tell you something. They use rubber bands now, sweetheart.
Yeah, why do they use them?

Sometimes, I mean, the spring breaks (inaudible) times on their horns and they use them until they can get springs to replace them, until they can get to someplace where they can fix them, find some springs.
